evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx:56-72 — confirmDelete (line 58 `await deleteRule.mutateAsync(deleteConfirm.id)`), handleToggle (line 64 `await updateRule.mutateAsync(...)`) and handleRun (line 71 `await runRule.mutateAsync(rule.id)`) all call mutateAsync with NO try/catch. mutateAsync returns a rejecting promise on failure, so any backend/network error becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

The page never surfaces these mutation errors to the user: grep for updateRule.error / deleteRule.error / runRule.error (and .isError) in the file returns nothing — only the *query* error is rendered ({error} at line 178, from useAutomationRules). So a failed delete/enable-toggle/run silently does nothing on-screen: confirmDelete's `setDeleteConfirm(null)` at line 59 never runs (modal sticks) and the toggle switch visually reverts with no explanation. Contrast EditRulePage.tsx:113 which does render {updateRule.error}. Fix: wrap each handler in try/catch (or use .mutate with onError) and render the mutation error states.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/ExecutionMonitoringPage.tsx:74-77 — handleRetry does `await retryExecution.mutateAsync(log.id); setSelectedLog(null);` with no try/catch. On a failed retry the mutateAsync promise rejects (unhandled rejection) and setSelectedLog(null) never fires, so the details modal stays open with no error shown.

The page surfaces the *query* error (logsError rendered at line 189) but never renders retryExecution.error / retryExecution.isError (grep confirms no such reference), so the retry action has no failure feedback path. Same unhandled-mutation-rejection class as AutomationRulesPage. Fix: try/catch the retry and render retryExecution.error near the retry control.

All five workflow-automation page files hardcode user-facing English and import no useTranslation (verified: useTranslation count = 0 in AutomationRulesPage.tsx, ExecutionMonitoringPage.tsx, EditRulePage.tsx, CreateRulePage.tsx, TemplateLibraryPage.tsx). Examples: AutomationRulesPage.tsx:82 'Automation Rules', :84 'Create and manage automated workflows for your properties.', :101 'Create Rule', :306 'Delete'/'Deleting...'; ExecutionMonitoringPage.tsx:93 'Execution Monitoring', :95 'Monitor and troubleshoot your automation executions.'; EditRulePage.tsx:37 'Invalid rule ID.', :47 'Failed to load automation rule. Please try again.'

The app is react-i18next-enabled and sibling components in the SAME feature already use t() (RuleCard.tsx, RuleBuilder.tsx, TriggerSelector.tsx, ExecutionDetailsModal.tsx, TemplatePreviewModal.tsx), so these page-level strings are an inconsistent i18n gap — the pages are untranslatable while their child components are. Fix: wire useTranslation into the five pages and move the literals into the workflow-automation namespace.
